mission.cluster: D — continuation/recovery and durable audit primitives

adaptation: TypeScript -> ESM JavaScript. `decision-ledger.ts` is ported whole (validateLedgerEntry, appendToLedger, summarizeLedger) with its field bounds, its closed outcome/source lists and its duplicate-id refusal preserved one for one.

§36 of `candidate-gate.ts` is ported whole into guardian-gate.mjs (GUARDIAN_CHECKS, THEME_GUARDIAN_CHECKS, requiredGuardianChecks, evaluateGuardian, termsOf and the themeCheck helper). §35 of the same donor file is cluster B and lives in the sibling `task-lifecycle` module; the split is by mission cluster, not by donor file, and both halves cite the same donor.

The donor's ledger `outcome` vocabulary type was module-private; the constants DECISION_OUTCOMES / DECISION_SOURCES are exported here so a caller can enumerate the closed lists rather than re-typing them. The donor's own list contents are unchanged.
`AuditLedgerError` replaces the donor's bare `throw new Error(...)`. Every donor message string is kept verbatim so a caller matching on text still matches.
Deliberate detail preserved: `termsOf` uses `toLocaleLowerCase()` (not `toLowerCase()`), keeps runs of four or more alphanumerics and deduplicates exactly as the donor does.

`appendAllToLedger` and `entriesForTask` are thin conveniences over the ported reducer. `copyList` copies array arguments but passes a malformed non-array through untouched, so a spread can never turn an invalid entry into a valid one and the validator stays the single gate.
The donor's `GuardianCheckResult` / `GuardianVerdict` interfaces were type-only; the two factories here construct the same shapes.

`src/shared/recovery.ts` §33.1–§33.2 is ported whole in `recovery.mjs` (classifyFailure, planRecovery, advanceRecovery) with the CLASS_RULES ladder, its `requires` preconditions, its precedence, its confidence/severity table, its reasons, the RECOVERY_ORDER and THEME_RECOVERY_STEPS declarations and the per-class step budgets preserved one for one. The donor's `RecoveryPlan`, `RecoveryProgress`, `RecoveryStepPlan` and `HnsFallbackDecision` were interfaces with no runtime existence; nothing about them is re-declared here.

Shape placement: the §33 value vocabularies (FAILURE_CLASSES, FAILURE_SEVERITIES, VERIFICATION_GATES, RECOVERY_ORDER, THEME_RECOVERY_STEPS, RECOVERY_ATTEMPT_OUTCOMES) and the value shapes (WorkspaceFacts, FailureObservation, FailureClassification, RecoveryAttempt) live in `contracts.mjs` beside the module's other declared vocabularies, so the closed sets and the containers have exactly one home; `recovery.mjs` holds only behaviour and re-exports the three §33 vocabularies its own API is read through.

The donor's `VerificationGate` type import is dropped (a type cannot survive plain ESM, and this module imports no TypeScript). The ten gates it could hold are declared as VERIFICATION_GATES so the classifier's own gate fallback is enumerable and the shape validators can refuse a gate outside the donor union.

The donor's type-only shape annotations became factories (workspaceFacts, failureObservation, failureClassification, recoveryAttempt) plus assert helpers. The asserts are the module's own guard: they refuse a field that lies about its type (a string where a list belongs, a non-integer exit code, a confidence outside 0..1, a step or class outside the declared sets) without adding a rule the donor did not have.
`planRecovery` uses the ported `assertFailureClassification`, so a classification that is not one of §33.1's classes is refused rather than indexing RECOVERY_RULES and crashing on `undefined`.
knownDifferences: No durable store: the donor keeps the JSON store in `electron/commander/decision-ledger-store.ts` and this module, like the donor's own, is only the record model plus the append reducer. Persistence stays the caller's responsibility.
No fs, no git, no secret scanner, no requirement graph and no review pipeline. Every §36 observation is supplied by the caller; an omission becomes NOT_RUN rather than an inferred value.
The donor's §36 context can carry a requirement graph and a scope grant computed by other Boss subsystems; those subsystems are NOT migrated, so the caller must supply their outputs.
`candidateIdFor` (the candidate record's id) is NOT here. It belongs to §35 and lives with the lifecycle in `task-lifecycle`.

§33.3's HNS external-executor fallback is NOT ported: `planHnsFallback`, `recordHnsUsage`, `HNS_ROLES`, the `CapabilityGap` record, the max-consecutive-HNS ceiling and its improvement-backlog stage describe a named third-party product's invocation budget and integration wiring, not a recovery primitive. The recovery ladder keeps its `HNS_FALLBACK` rung and its `hns_allowed` decision, because those are §33.2's own ordering rules; what is left out is the external product's invocation policy, which belongs to whatever executor integration ever calls HNS. Carrying the budget here would put a vendor's rate limit inside the city's recovery model.
No clock. The donor's HNS path read `new Date(0).toISOString()` as its `now` default; no ported function needs a time input, so no function here takes one and no timestamp is produced anywhere.
No CapabilityGap and no improvisation record: both were only reachable through the HNS path, and neither is a §33.1/§33.2 recovery primitive.

vectors: every ledger field bound is enforced at its donor value: question 2000, 10 candidates of 200, chosen 2000, 50 evidence rows of 2000, rollback 2000, policy 200; the exact boundary values are accepted and one past them is refused
the outcome and source lists are closed: MAYBE and 'vibes' are refused
an invalid `createdAt` is refused by Date.parse, not accepted as a string
append returns a new array and never mutates the input; a duplicate id is refused rather than merged
summarizeLedger counts by source and outcome with every known source present at zero, and reports the ROLLED_BACK count as `rollbacks`
with no observations all seven checks are NOT_RUN, all seven are listed in `not_inspected` and in `blocking`, and the verdict is REPAIR with '0 check(s) failed, 7 could not be run'
a fully evidenced candidate is ACCEPTED with reason '§36 every required check passed (7)'
a destructive context carrying `unchecked` reasons yields NOT_RUN, never PASS, and blocks release
an unapproved removal fails and names the removal kind (file/test/script); an approved one does not
requirement coverage below 100% fails and reports the ratio; the empty-required case is 100%
an empty goal, and a deliverable with no serving requirement, each fail GOAL_COMPLIANCE
a file written outside the grant, and a refused change unit, each fail SCOPE_VALIDATION
a zero-row evidence ledger fails EVIDENCE_COMPLETENESS even with nothing outstanding; an uncovered review fails it too
an Owner override is matched lexically against the obligations and fails when fewer than half of its significant terms appear
a touched theme lane requires the four theme checks even when no package was read; with theme_required and no packages the verdict is REPAIR with '4 could not be run'
a clean readable theme package set yields 11 passing checks; a dirty one fails isolation, fallback, executable-payload and built-in integrity
a non-built-in theme is not judged on built-in integrity
termsOf lower-cases, keeps runs of four or more alphanumerics and deduplicates

§33.1 declares exactly thirteen failure classes in the donor order (TRANSIENT … UNKNOWN) and four severities; §33.2 declares exactly seven ladder steps (NATIVE_RETRY … HARD_BLOCKER) and three theme steps (DISABLE_THEME, FALLBACK_BUILT_IN_THEME, RECORD_DIAGNOSTIC)

every one of the twelve non-UNKNOWN classes is produced by its own observation with the donor's exact confidence, severity, reason string and signals: TRANSIENT 0.7/LOW, TERMINAL 1/CRITICAL, DEPENDENCY 0.9/MEDIUM, AUTH 0.95/HIGH, RATE_LIMIT 0.95/MEDIUM, PROVIDER_PAGE 0.9/MEDIUM, WORKSPACE 0.9/HIGH, BUILD 0.85/MEDIUM, TEST 0.85/MEDIUM, ENVIRONMENT 0.85/HIGH, THEME 0.9/MEDIUM, UI 0.85/MEDIUM

precedence is most-authoritative-first: a Guardian denial outranks the timeout in the same output; a policy_refusal carried in its own field outranks any prose and reports `policy_refusal:<text>` as its only signal; AUTH outranks RATE_LIMIT; PAGE_CHANGED outranks ECONNRESET; a missing module outranks the word `sandbox`; the UI rule outranks the THEME rule

a rule with a `requires` precondition does not fire when the host fact is absent: `Cannot find module` with `missing_modules: []` is UNKNOWN, `escapes workspace` with no scope fact is UNKNOWN, a theme diagnostic with no counted diagnostics is not THEME, `overflow` with `visual_failed: false` is UNKNOWN; each becomes its real class once the precondition holds
TS2307 is a DEPENDENCY (it is on the donor's DEPENDENCY pattern list) while a non-2307 `error TS<digits>` is a BUILD

a gate with no recognisable signature is classified from the gate at confidence 0.5 and signal `gate:<gate>` (SYNTAX/TYPECHECK/BUILD→BUILD, UNIT/MODULE/INTEGRATION/FULL→TEST, VISUAL/RUNTIME/BLACKBOX→UI); a gate outside that map, such as BENCHMARK, is UNKNOWN at 0.3 with the §33.1-has-no-class reason; an observation with nothing at all is UNKNOWN at 0.1 with no signals, and an exit code alone is not a signal
at most three matched patterns are reported as signals, in donor pattern order, and the classifier reads runtime_code and semantic_outcome as well as detail

the plan for every class lists all seven ladder steps in RECOVERY_ORDER, marks each applicable step with the donor budget, marks each other step inapplicable with its donor reason (never dropping it), and ends with HARD_BLOCKER applicable at budget 1 with `ends_at_hard_blocker: true`, `schemaVersion: 1` and `version: 'recovery-1'`

the plan's applicable budgets are the donor's per-class table: TRANSIENT 2/1, DEPENDENCY 2/1 (local/alternate-internal), AUTH alternate-provider 1, RATE_LIMIT 1/2/1, PROVIDER_PAGE 2/1/1, WORKSPACE local 2, BUILD local 3, TEST local 3, ENVIRONMENT 2/1, THEME 2/1, UI local 3, UNKNOWN 1/1/1 — plus HNS at 1 wherever `hns_allowed` is true

`next` is the first applicable step that is not HARD_BLOCKER, so TERMINAL has no `next` and produces the diagnostic 'no recovery step applies; the plan goes straight to the Hard Blocker'; `hns_allowed` is false exactly for TERMINAL, AUTH and WORKSPACE, and where it is false HNS_FALLBACK carries '§33.3: HNS is not a recovery route for this failure class'
`requires_owner` is set only for TERMINAL (AUTHORIZATION, policy), WORKSPACE (AUTHORIZATION, scope) and AUTH (SIGN_IN), with the donor's own reasons; every other class has none
only THEME carries `theme_steps` (the three-step ladder) and the theme diagnostic; every other class has no `theme_steps` and no diagnostics

progress counts attempts per step ignoring NOT_APPLICABLE, offers attempt `used + 1 of budget` while `used < budget`, and at the exact budget boundary moves to the next applicable step: TRANSIENT goes NATIVE_RETRY 1/2 → 2/2 → LOCAL_RECOVERY 1/1 → HNS_FALLBACK 1/1 → Hard Blocker
HNS cannot be reached while any cheaper applicable step still has budget, and attempting a later step does not advance the run past an unspent earlier one
a PASS spends budget exactly as a FAIL does, because the run advances on attempts made

total exhaustion reports `exhausted: true`, `hard_blocker: true` and '§33.2 Hard Blocker: every applicable recovery step is exhausted'; a class with no applicable step reports '§33.2 Hard Blocker: no step applies (<first skipped step's reason>)'
a TERMINAL plan offers no retry at all: its only applicable step is HARD_BLOCKER, and advanceRecovery returns no `next` even after attempts at NATIVE_RETRY and HNS_FALLBACK are recorded

the shape factories build the donor shapes (missing fields present as undefined, lists copied) and the assert helpers refuse a string where a list belongs, a non-integer exit code, a gate outside the donor union, a class or severity outside §33.1's sets, a confidence outside 0..1 or non-finite, and a step or outcome outside §33.2's sets

PARITY: the ledger's field bounds, closed vocabularies and error messages
all seven §36 checks and their pass/fail reason strings
NOT_RUN-as-blocker and the ACCEPTED/REPAIR verdict derivation
the lexical Owner-override matching rule and its half-terms threshold
the four theme checks and their required-when-touched rule
§33.1's thirteen-class ladder, its `requires` preconditions, its precedence, and every confidence, severity and reason string
§33.1's gate fallback and the UNKNOWN-not-guessed rule for a gate §33.1 has no class for
§33.2's RECOVERY_ORDER, THEME_RECOVERY_STEPS, per-class applicability, budgets, inapplicable reasons and `next` selection
§33.2's advanceRecovery budget, exhaustion, next-step and Hard-Blocker semantics, including that a terminal failure is never planned for retry
PORT_ADAPTATION: AuditLedgerError in place of bare Error, with donor messages preserved
the closed lists exported as constants
copy-on-construct factories in place of donor interfaces

the donor's §33 type-only import (VerificationGate) is replaced by the VERIFICATION_GATES constant, and its type-only shapes (WorkspaceFacts, FailureObservation, FailureClassification, RecoveryPlan, RecoveryAttempt, RecoveryProgress) by factories/validators in contracts.mjs plus plain object construction in recovery.mjs
the §33 vocabularies live in contracts.mjs so the closed sets and containers have one home, with recovery.mjs holding the behaviour and re-exporting the three vocabularies its API is read through
planRecovery validates its classification through the ported assert, so an unknown class is refused instead of crashing on an undefined rule
UTOPIA_EXTENSION: DECISION_OUTCOMES / DECISION_SOURCES / CHECK_VERDICTS / GUARDIAN_VERDICTS exported as enumerable constants; they describe the donor's own closed sets and add no member.
entriesForTask: a filter over the ported ledger for the Owner's per-task audit view.

FAILURE_CLASSES / FAILURE_SEVERITIES / VERIFICATION_GATES / RECOVERY_ORDER / THEME_RECOVERY_STEPS / RECOVERY_ATTEMPT_OUTCOMES and the shape asserts are exported for the same reason: they describe the donor's own closed sets and add no member.
DEFERRED: any requirement graph, scope grant, secret scanner or review pipeline that feeds §36
the donor's broader evidence-ledger and coordination-ledger modules (they value-import execution-planner, requirements-graph and the tenx knowledge module, which are outside this cluster's boundary)

§33.3's HNS external-executor fallback: planHnsFallback, recordHnsUsage, HNS_ROLES, the CapabilityGap record, MAX_CONSECUTIVE_HNS_CALLS and the improvement-backlog stage. It is a named third-party product's invocation budget and integration wiring, not a recovery primitive, and it is outside this module's boundary; the ladder's HNS_FALLBACK rung and its `hns_allowed` decision are kept because they are §33.2's own ordering rules.
